questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: EXONERATE
questions.x: 'Exonerate' is the opposite of 'Convict'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Exonerate'.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To show the white feather' mean?
questions.x: 'To show the white feather' means: to show cowardice.

questions.q: Had the employer deposited the dues on time, the workers ____ penalised.
questions.x: Correct answer: would not have been. Inverted third conditional.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'Government by the wealthy'
questions.x: 'Plutocracy' means government by the wealthy.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'A red-letter day' mean?
questions.x: 'A red-letter day' means: a memorable or important day.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: AMELIORATE
questions.x: 'Ameliorate' means improve. 'Worsen' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: COGENT
questions.x: 'Cogent' means convincing. 'Weak' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The number of claims / received this month / are higher than last month.
questions.x: The error is in part (c): 'are higher than last month'. 'The number of' takes a singular verb: 'is higher'.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: MAGNANIMOUS
questions.x: 'Magnanimous' is the opposite of 'Petty'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Magnanimous'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The accounts department / has been asked / to reconcile the balances by Monday.
o: to reconcile the balances by Monday.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. The sentence is correct.

questions.q: According to the passage, the success of a health campaign is measured by:
questions.x: Answer: 'Changes in behaviour'. The opening sentence states this. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: The success of a public health campaign is measured not by the number of posters printed but by changes in behaviour. Handwashing campaigns that rely only on messages often fade, while those that also place soap and water where people need them last longer. Convenience, reminders and social example make healthy choices the easy choices. Policy works best when it designs the environment, not just the slogan.

questions.q: Which statement best summarises the passage?
o: Soap is too expensive for campaigns
Slogans are the most effective tool
Making healthy choices convenient works better than messages alone
questions.x: Answer: 'Making healthy choices convenient works better than messages alone'. The passage contrasts messages with environmental design. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: The success of a public health campaign is measured not by the number of posters printed but by changes in behaviour. Handwashing campaigns that rely only on messages often fade, while those that also place soap and water where people need them last longer. Convenience, reminders and social example make healthy choices the easy choices. Policy works best when it designs the environment, not just the slogan.

questions.q: The Federal Court of India, established under the 1935 Act, began functioning in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1937. It was succeeded by the Supreme Court in 1950.

questions.q: The Vaikom Satyagraha against untouchability began — this happened in the year:
questions.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha against untouchability began in 1924. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1937 session of the Indian National Congress held at Faizpur?
questions.x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the 1937 Faizpur session — the first session held in a village.

questions.q: The Deccan Riots of 1875 were directed mainly against:
questions.x: Correct answer: Marwari and Gujarati moneylenders. They led to the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879.

questions.q: Gandhi called off the Civil Disobedience Movement and signed a pact with Lord Irwin in:
questions.x: Political prisoners not convicted of violence were released; Congress agreed to attend the Second RTC.

questions.q: Who founded the India House, London?
questions.x: The India House, London was founded by Shyamji Krishna Varma.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Poona Pact 2. Gandhi–Irwin Pact 3. Dandi March 4. Communal Award
questions.x: Dandi March (March 1930), Gandhi–Irwin Pact (March 1931), Communal Award (August 1932), Poona Pact (September 1932).

questions.q: The newspaper/journal 'Mooknayak' is associated with:
questions.x: 'Mooknayak' was started/edited by B. R. Ambedkar.

questions.q: The Bengal Famine of 1943 occurred during the viceroyalty of:
o: Lord Linlithgow (and continued under Lord Wavell)
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Linlithgow (and continued under Lord Wavell). Around three million people died.

questions.q: The book 'The Economic History of India' was written by:
questions.x: 'The Economic History of India' was written by R. C. Dutt.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Millets are called 'climate-resilient' crops.
Reason (R): They need less water and can grow in poor soils and high temperatures.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: The new Pope elected in May 2025, the first from the United States, took the name:
questions.x: Correct answer: Leo XIV. Cardinal Robert Prevost succeeded Pope Francis.

questions.q: The 'Emissions Gap Report' is published by:
questions.x: 'Emissions Gap Report' is brought out by UN Environment Programme.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Nomadic Elephant' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Nomadic Elephant' is a bilateral exercise between India and Mongolia.

questions.q: The 'BioE3' policy approved in 2024 stands for:
o: Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment
Bio-fuels for Electricity, Engines and Electronics
questions.x: Correct answer: Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment. It promotes high-performance biomanufacturing.

questions.q: India won the Thomas Cup (badminton) for the first time in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 2022. India defeated Indonesia in the final in Bangkok.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in The Hague?
o: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
questions.x: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons is based in The Hague.

questions.q: The QUAD grouping comprises India, the USA, Japan and:
questions.x: Correct answer: Australia. It focuses on a free and open Indo-Pacific.

questions.q: The 'Ayushman Vay Vandana Card' is issued to:
o: Senior citizens aged 70 and above under PM-JAY
questions.x: Correct answer: Senior citizens aged 70 and above under PM-JAY. It provides health cover of up to ₹5 lakh a year.

questions.q: World Water Day is observed on:
questions.x: World Water Day: 22 March.

questions.q: The Constitution (31st Amendment) Act, 1973:
o: Added the Ninth Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review
Sought to establish the National Judicial Appointments Commission (later struck down)
Raised the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545
Added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble and inserted Fundamental Duties
questions.x: The 31st Amendment (1973) raised the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545.

questions.q: Article 239AA of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Special provisions with respect to Delhi
Early childhood care and education for children below six years
Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession
questions.x: Article 239AA: Special provisions with respect to Delhi.

questions.q: Who certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.x: Correct answer: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha. The Speaker's decision is final under Article 110(3).

questions.q: Article 265 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Taxes not to be imposed save by authority of law
Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People
Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession
questions.x: Article 265: Taxes not to be imposed save by authority of law.

questions.q: The GST Council is chaired by:
questions.x: State Finance Ministers are members; decisions need three-fourths of weighted votes.

questions.q: Section 66A of the IT Act, 2000 was struck down as violative of Article 19(1)(a) in:
o: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
questions.x: Correct answer: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015). The Court held the provision vague and overbroad.

questions.q: The election of the President is held in accordance with:
o: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, by secret ballot
questions.x: Correct answer: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, by secret ballot. Article 55 provides for uniformity and parity of representation.

questions.q: President's Rule under Article 356 can be continued for a maximum of:
o: Three years, with parliamentary approval every six months
questions.x: Correct answer: Three years, with parliamentary approval every six months. Beyond one year, conditions under Article 356(5) apply.

questions.q: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, renamed the principal Act as:
o: Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development (UMEED) Act
questions.x: Parliament passed it in April 2025; several provisions were challenged in the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The 'PESA Act, 1996' extends Panchayati Raj provisions to:
o: Fifth Schedule areas, with special powers to Gram Sabhas
questions.x: The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act empowers Gram Sabhas over minor forest produce, land alienation etc.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 8% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹300 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.08 = 12.5.
Total deposits = 300 × 12.5 = ₹3,750 crore (of which new credit = ₹3,450 crore).

questions.q: The global Multidimensional Poverty Index is published by UNDP and:
o: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)
questions.x: Correct answer: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI). It uses health, education and standard of living dimensions.

questions.q: The 'National Infrastructure Pipeline' (2019) was launched to:
o: Project infrastructure investment across sectors over 2020–25
questions.x: Correct answer: Project infrastructure investment across sectors over 2020–25. It envisaged investment of about ₹111 lakh crore.

questions.q: "Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth" was the focus of which plan?
questions.x: It was the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–17).

questions.q: Which committee/body is associated with "Agricultural credit system"?
questions.x: A. M. Khusro Committee (1989) dealt with agricultural credit system.

questions.q: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961, comes into force from:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1 April 2026. It simplifies the language and structure of the direct tax law.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign exchange reserves:
1. They include foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position with the IMF.
2. They are managed by the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
The RBI manages forex reserves under the RBI Act.

questions.q: The Food Corporation of India was set up in 1965 under the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Food Corporations Act, 1964. It procures, stores and distributes foodgrains for the PDS.

questions.q:
In which year did the following happen?
The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) was set up.
questions.x: The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) was set up in 1990.

questions.q: 'Twin balance sheet problem' refers to stress in the balance sheets of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Banks and corporates. The Economic Survey 2016–17 discussed it.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹70,000 is depreciated at 25% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 70,000 × (0.75)^3 = ₹29,531.25.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹17,500.)

questions.q: A firm earns an average profit of ₹1,24,800 on capital employed of ₹8,90,000. The normal rate of return in the industry is 12%. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit is:
The ratio in which old partners surrender their share of profit in favour of a new partner is the:
questions.x: Sacrificing ratio = old ratio − new ratio.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹76,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹3,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹4,000; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹250; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹600. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹76,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 3,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 4,000
− Bank charges 250
+ Interest credited 600
Pass book balance = ₹75,850.

questions.q: Events occurring after the balance sheet date that provide evidence of conditions existing at that date are called:
questions.x: Adjusting events (e.g., debtor's insolvency known after year-end) require adjustment of amounts.

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹3,60,000 and at the end ₹4,87,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹40,000 and withdrew ₹2,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 4,87,500 + 2,500 − 40,000 − 3,60,000 = ₹90,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: Earnings per share (EPS) is computed as:
o: Profit available to equity shareholders ÷ Number of equity shares
Net profit ÷ Total shares including preference
questions.x: Correct answer: Profit available to equity shareholders ÷ Number of equity shares. Preference dividend is deducted from profit before dividing.

questions.q: A bad debt written off in an earlier year is recovered in cash. The entry is:
o: Debtor's A/c Dr. To Bad Debts Recovered A/c
Cash A/c Dr. To Debtor's A/c
Bad Debts A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Cash A/c Dr. To Bad Debts Recovered A/c
questions.x: The debtor's account is closed; recovery is a gain credited to Bad Debts Recovered A/c.

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹35,000, closing inventory is ₹25,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹2,40,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (35,000 + 25,000) / 2 = ₹30,000.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 2,40,000 / 30,000 = 8 times.

questions.q: A provision for discount on debtors is usually calculated on:
o: Debtors after deducting bad debts and provision for doubtful debts
questions.x: Correct answer: Debtors after deducting bad debts and provision for doubtful debts. Discount is expected only from good debtors.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Drawings by the proprietor are deducted from capital.
Reason (R): Drawings are an expense charged to the profit and loss account.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is true. R is false: drawings are not a business expense; they reduce capital directly.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹18,000; selling price ₹205 and variable cost ₹190 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹10,500?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (18,000 + 10,500) / 15 = 1,900 units.

questions.q: Noting charges paid on dishonour of a bill are ultimately borne by:
o: The drawee (acceptor), being debited to his account
questions.x: Correct answer: The drawee (acceptor), being debited to his account. Noting charges are debited to the party liable — the acceptor.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹14; 10th — 250 units @ ₹17; 20th — 300 units @ ₹21. 500 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 250 units left come from the latest purchases: 250 × ₹21 = ₹5,250.

questions.q: Under the OSH Code, an employer must report to the authorities any accident at the workplace causing death or serious bodily injury:
o: Only if the worker's family complains
Only once a year in the annual return
questions.x: Notice of accidents and dangerous occurrences must be sent to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator and other authorities as prescribed.

questions.q: The IR Code empowers the appropriate government to increase the threshold of 300 workers for prior permission for lay-off, retrenchment and closure:
o: Only with the consent of all trade unions
Only by amending the Code in Parliament
Only with the consent of the ILO
questions.x: Section 77 allows the threshold to be raised by notification of the appropriate government.

questions.q: Victor Vroom's expectancy theory explains motivation as a product of:
questions.x: Motivation = Expectancy × Instrumentality × Valence. ERG is Alderfer; power/affiliation/achievement is McClelland.

questions.q: Which category of workers was specifically covered by the Motor Transport Workers Act, 1961?
o: Workers in motor transport undertakings such as bus and truck operators
questions.x: The Act regulated conditions of work of motor transport workers; it is subsumed in the OSH Code.

questions.q: The 'universality test' for including an allowance in basic wages for EPF purposes was first laid down in:
o: Kichha Sugar Co. v. Tarai Chini Mill Mazdoor Union (2014)
Bridge and Roof Co. (India) Ltd v. Union of India (1963)
Jay Engineering Works v. Union of India (1963)
questions.x: Bridge and Roof (1963) held that payments made to all employees as a class are part of basic wages, while incentive payments linked to extra work are not.

questions.q: The expert committee (2019) that recommended a need-based national minimum wage of ₹375 per day (July 2018 prices) was headed by:
questions.x: The Satpathy Committee also recommended an additional city compensatory allowance of up to ₹55 per day for urban workers.

questions.q: Which case laid down that the definition of 'workman' depends on the main or predominant duties performed and not on designation?
o: S.K. Maini v. Carona Sahu Co. (1994)
questions.x: The Court looks at the dominant nature of duties to decide whether a person is a workman.

questions.q: A firm pays basic ₹12,000, DA ₹3,000, HRA ₹12,000, conveyance allowance ₹5,000 and sales commission ₹8,000 (total ₹40,000) a month. Under the Code on Wages' 50% rule, the amount treated as 'wages' is:
questions.x: Wages (basic + DA) = ₹15,000. HRA, conveyance and commission are excluded items totalling ₹25,000, which exceed 50% of ₹40,000 (₹20,000) by ₹5,000. That excess is added back: wages = ₹15,000 + ₹5,000 = ₹20,000. (An allowance not in the exclusion list would simply be part of wages.)

questions.q: The ILO supervisory body that examines government reports on ratified conventions, consisting of independent jurists, is the:
o: Committee of Experts on the Application of Conventions and Recommendations (CEACR)
questions.x: CEACR, created in 1926, examines reports; the Committee on Freedom of Association examines complaints even against non-ratifying states.

questions.q: If a contractor fails to pay the minimum wages due to contract workers, the Code on Wages makes whom liable to pay the unpaid amount?
questions.x: Section 17(5) obliges the company/firm/establishment (principal employer) to pay if the contractor fails, with the right to recover from the contractor.

questions.q: The 'Kanpur Mazdoor Sabha' and the 'Meerut Conspiracy Case' (1929) are associated with:
o: The rise of communist-led labour activism
questions.x: The Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929) prosecuted trade unionists and communists for organising railway and textile workers.

questions.q: 'Social security and social insurance; employment and unemployment' is a subject in which entry of the Concurrent List?
questions.x: Entry 22: trade unions, industrial and labour disputes; Entry 23: social security and social insurance, employment and unemployment; Entry 24: welfare of labour.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, a disciplinary inquiry against a suspended worker should ordinarily be completed within:
questions.x: The Code expects the inquiry to be completed ordinarily within ninety days.

questions.q: For permanent total disablement under the Employees' Compensation Act, compensation equals what percentage of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor?
questions.x: Permanent total disablement: 60% of monthly wages × relevant factor, subject to a prescribed minimum.

questions.q: Under the OSH Code, a contractor engaging contract labour must obtain a licence. One feature of the Code is:
o: Licence issued only by the ILO
A single licence for undertaking work in more than one State or for the whole country
questions.x: The OSH Code provides for a single licence (for work in more than one State or across India), replacing work-order-wise licences.

questions.q: A worker engaged on a weekly wage period must be paid under the Code on Wages:
o: On the first working day of the next week
Within 7 days after the week ends
On the last working day of the week, before the weekly holiday
questions.x: Weekly wages are due on the last working day of the week, i.e., before the weekly holiday.

questions.q: Under ESI, 'employment injury' includes an accident while commuting to or from work if:
o: It is related to employment as per the extended definition, subject to conditions
It happens on a holiday trip
questions.x: Commuting accidents were brought within employment injury (with conditions) by amendment, mirroring the Code's approach.

questions.q: An employer can be exempted from EDLI under Section 17(2A) if it:
o: Provides a group insurance scheme with benefits more favourable than EDLI
questions.x: Exemption requires life insurance benefits not less favourable than those under the EDLI Scheme.

questions.q: From January 2024, free foodgrains under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana were extended for how long?
questions.x: The Government decided to provide free foodgrains to NFSA beneficiaries for five years from 1 January 2024.

questions.q:
The reduced EPF contribution rate of 10% applies to which of the following?
1. Establishments employing less than 20 employees
2. Units in the jute, beedi, brick, coir and guar gum industries
3. All establishments in the IT sector
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The 10% rate applies to establishments with fewer than 20 employees, sick industrial companies, and jute, beedi, brick, coir and guar gum industries. IT establishments pay 12%.

questions.q: Which scheme replaced the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY), a health insurance scheme for BPL families launched in 2008?
questions.x: RSBY (₹30,000 cover, under the Labour Ministry) was subsumed into PM-JAY in 2018.

questions.q: EPF's 'Nidhi Aapke Nikat 2.0' programme is:
o: A district-level outreach and grievance redressal camp held monthly
questions.x: Under Nidhi Aapke Nikat 2.0 (2023), EPFO and ESIC hold monthly outreach camps in every district.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. MGNREGA is a demand-driven, legally guaranteed employment programme.
2. Wages under MGNREGA are paid by the employer who hires the workers.
3. MGNREGA wage rates are notified by the Central Government for each State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Wages are paid by the Government (largely central funds) directly to workers' accounts; there is no private employer. Rates are notified by the Centre State-wise.

questions.q: Which document must EPS pensioners submit annually to continue receiving pension?
o: Life certificate (physical or digital Jeevan Pramaan)
questions.x: Pensioners submit a life certificate once a year; Jeevan Pramaan (2014) enables digital submission.

questions.q: Under IGNOAPS, the central assistance to BPL persons aged 80 and above is:
questions.x: Central assistance is ₹200 per month for ages 60–79 and ₹500 for 80+; States add top-ups.

questions.q: An employee whose average daily wage is ₹168 works in an ESI-covered factory and earns ₹17,000 in a month. Which statement about the month's contribution is correct?
o: Neither pays, as low-wage employees are excluded from coverage
Only the employer pays 3.25% (≈ ₹553); the employee's share is exempt
questions.x: Employees whose average daily wage is up to ₹176 are exempt from paying their own 0.75% share, but they remain covered and the employer must still pay 3.25% of wages. Here employer share ≈ ₹553.

questions.q: An employee retires after 20 years and 5 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹85,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
5 months is not more than six months, so it is ignored → 20 years.
= 15/26 × 85,000 × 20 = ₹9,80,769 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q: An employee's basic + DA is ₹13,000 a month. The employer's monthly EPS contribution is:
Why does ice float on water?
o: Ice is less dense than water
questions.x: Water expands on freezing; this anomalous expansion protects aquatic life in winter.

questions.q: A hydrometer is used to measure:
questions.x: Hydrometer: Relative density of liquids.

questions.q: LED bulbs are more energy-efficient than incandescent bulbs because they:
o: Convert more electricity into light rather than heat
questions.x: Correct answer: Convert more electricity into light rather than heat. BEE star labels indicate energy efficiency.

questions.q: The causative agent of diphtheria is:
o: Chikungunya virus (an alphavirus spread by Aedes mosquitoes)
Wuchereria bancrofti (nematode worm, spread by Culex mosquitoes)
questions.x: Diphtheria: Corynebacterium diphtheriae (bacterium).

questions.q: 'Open-source software' is software whose:
o: Source code is freely available to use, modify and distribute
questions.x: Correct answer: Source code is freely available to use, modify and distribute. Examples include Linux, LibreOffice and Firefox.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Pressure cookers cook food faster.
Reason (R): Increased pressure raises the boiling point of water.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Higher boiling point means higher cooking temperature.

questions.q: The device that converts solar energy directly into electricity is a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Photovoltaic (solar) cell. Solar cells are usually made of silicon semiconductors.

questions.q: 'Internet of Things' refers to:
o: Everyday devices connected to the internet to collect and exchange data
questions.x: Correct answer: Everyday devices connected to the internet to collect and exchange data. Smart meters and wearables are examples.

questions.q: In computing, 'GUI' stands for:
questions.x: GUI = Graphical User Interface.

questions.q: F5 key in most web browsers is used to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Refresh the page. F1 usually opens help.

questions.q: Chandrasekhar limit is credited to:
questions.x: Chandrasekhar limit: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar.

questions.q: Antibiotics are effective against:
questions.x: They do not work against viral infections like the common cold; misuse causes antimicrobial resistance.

questions.q: In a row, Deepak is 14th from the left and Rekha is 7th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Deepak becomes 28th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Deepak occupies Rekha's old place, which is 7th from the right and now 28th from the left.
Total = 28 + 7 − 1 = 34.

questions.q: ₹34,000 is invested for 1 year at 10% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 10/2 = 5%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 34,000 × (1 + 5/100)² = ₹37,485.
CI = ₹3,485 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹3,400).

questions.q: The number of claims settled by a regional office rises by 10%, then falls by 10%, and finally rises by 20%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 10/100) × (1 − 10/100) × (1 + 20/100) = 1.1 × 0.9 × 1.2 = 1.188.
Overall change = (1.188 − 1) × 100 = 18.8% → 18.8% increase.
Note: simply adding (10 − 10 + 20) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 28 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 14 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(12, 28, 14) = 84 units.
Rates: +7, +3, −6 units/hour → net 4 units/hour.
Time = 84 / 4 = 21 hours.

questions.q: A field officer starts from point O and walks 9 km towards South, then turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 5 km, and finally turns left and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -9 +5 = -4 km → 4 km South.
East–West: +12 -9 = 3 km → 3 km East.
Distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, towards South-East.

questions.q: A vessel holds 200 litres of pure milk. 20 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 200 × (1 − 20/200)² = 200 × (0.9)² = 162 litres.
Removing 2 × 20 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into cones of base radius 1 cm and height 2 cm. How many cones are obtained?
questions.x:
Number = volume of sphere / volume of one cone = (4/3)πR³ / ((1/3)πr²h)
= 4R³ / (r²h) = 4 × 6³ / (1² × 2) = 864 / 2 = 432.

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹55,000. B joins after 6 months with ₹15,000, and C joins after 6 months with ₹35,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹38,400, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 55,000×12, B: 15,000×6, C: 35,000×6 → 22 : 3 : 7.
B's share = 3/32 × 38,400 = ₹3,600.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 536, 782, 1274 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 782 − 536 = 246, 1274 − 782 = 492.
HCF(246, 492) = 246.

questions.q: The present ages of a mother and her son are in the ratio 9 : 5. 10 years ago, the ratio was 17 : 5. What is the son's present age?
questions.x:
Let ages be 9k and 5k.
(9k − 10) / (5k − 10) = 17/5 → k = 3.
Son = 5 × 3 = 15 years.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 8 : 5 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 5 : 2. If each of them saves ₹18,000 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 8k, 5k and expenditures = 5m, 2m.
8k − 5m = 5k − 2m = 18,000 → 3k = 3m.
Solving gives k = 6,000, m = 6,000.
P's income = 8 × 6,000 = ₹48,000 (check: ₹48,000 − ₹30,000 = ₹18,000).

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2019: 230  |  2020: 265  |  2021: 290  |  2022: 280  |  2023: 295.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2020: 15.22%; 2021: 9.43%; 2022: -3.45%; 2023: 5.36%.
Highest growth: 2020 (15.22%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 113, 97, 95 and 163.
questions.x: 97, 113, 163 are all prime numbers; 95 is not. Hence 95 is the odd one out.

questions.q: At what time between 1 and 2 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.x:
At 1:00 the minute hand is 5 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To coincide it must gain 5 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 5 × 60/55 = 60/11 minutes = 5 5/11 minutes past 1.
